facts.value: Competency requirements may be met with high school work, college work or test scores. These requirements must be met regardless of your major or the number of transferable hours you have earned.

source.title: How to meet ASU course competency requirements + English competency requirement

facts.value: Students must earn a minimum 2.00 GPA in each competency area.

source.title: How to meet ASU course competency requirements + English competency requirement

facts.value: Admission may be granted with one deficiency in no more than two competency areas. Deficiencies in both math and laboratory science are not acceptable.

source.title: How to meet ASU course competency requirements + English competency requirement

facts.value: Meet one of the following: Four years of high school English (composition- or literature-based); Minimum test score of 21 on ACT English, or 580 on SAT evidence-based reading and writing; One transferable 3-credit college English composition course.

source.title: How to meet ASU course competency requirements + English competency requirement

facts.value: All new students will be placed in First-Year Composition ENG 101. Students whose native language is not English will be enrolled in ENG 107. Enrollment in ENG 105, Advanced First Year composition, is based on placement test scores.

source.title: English composition placement + Mathematics competency requirement

facts.value: If you have college-level transfer credit or test credit equivalent to ASU’s first year composition course(s), that credit will be considered in placement.

source.title: English composition placement + Mathematics competency requirement

facts.value: You can search ASU’s equivalency database for transfer credit at tcg.asu.edu.

source.title: English composition placement + Mathematics competency requirement

facts.value: Meet one of the following: Four years of high school courses: one year each of algebra I, geometry, algebra II and an advanced math class for which algebra II is a prerequisite; Minimum test score of 24 on ACT math, or 580 on SAT math; One transferable 3-credit college math course for which at least intermediate algebra is a prerequisite.

source.title: English composition placement + Mathematics competency requirement

facts.value: Students may meet any one or a combination of the following options, provided that three distinct laboratory-based science courses are completed with a 2.00 unweighted GPA or higher.

source.title: Laboratory science competency requirement

facts.value: Three years of high school laboratory sciences in three different subject areas, preferably biology, chemistry, earth science or physics.

source.title: Laboratory science competency requirement

facts.value: A laboratory-based integrated science course may be allowed to substitute for one of the three lab sciences. Each course should be one year in length.

source.title: Laboratory science competency requirement

facts.value: A laboratory-based advanced science course may be allowed to substitute for one of the three lab sciences. An advanced science class is a lab science that is generally taken in the last two years of high school and is at least one of the following: an advanced placement course, a higher-level international baccalaureate course, a dual enrollment course, or other honors course for which the previous lab science course is a prerequisite.

source.title: Laboratory science competency requirement

facts.value: Minimum test scores in three standardized tests from three different subject matters. The following tests may be taken: SAT II subject test score in chemistry-600, biology-590, physics-620 or ACT test score in science-20.

source.title: Laboratory science competency requirement

facts.value: Three transferable 4-credit college laboratory science courses from the following: biology, chemistry, earth science or physics. An integrated laboratory science or advanced-level laboratory-based science may be substituted for one of these laboratory subjects.

source.title: Laboratory science competency requirement

facts.value: Students are required to complete three different lab sciences.

source.title: Laboratory Science Courses (for online high schools only) + Second language competency requirement

facts.value: If lab sciences do not meet the requirement, students may need to provide additional information through a Priority Task displayed on My ASU called Course Description.

source.title: Laboratory Science Courses (for online high schools only) + Second language competency requirement

facts.value: Students can have their high school submit their lab sciences to the courseapproval.asu.edu website for ASU review or submit a course description form for each lab science taken.

source.title: Laboratory Science Courses (for online high schools only) + Second language competency requirement

facts.value: Students must meet one of the following: two years of the same high school second language, a minimum score on a national standardized second language test, placement into a third semester college second language class based on university placement exam results, or completion of two transferable 3- or 4-credit college-level courses in the same second language.

source.title: Laboratory Science Courses (for online high schools only) + Second language competency requirement

facts.value: One year of high school American history.

source.title: Social science competency requirement + Fine arts or career and technical education competency requirement

facts.value: Minimum SAT II subject test score of 560 on American history/social studies.

source.title: Social science competency requirement + Fine arts or career and technical education competency requirement

facts.value: One transferable 3-credit college American history course.
